provenance: IBM AMLworld HI-Small. Altman et al., 'Realistic Synthetic Financial Transactions for Anti-Money Laundering Models', NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks. Data: IBM Transactions for Anti-Money Laundering (AML), CDLA-Sharing-1.0. The corpus is entirely SYNTHETIC by IBM's own statement, generated by a multi-agent virtual world, not real customer data; what is real is the provenance, not the transactions. These are 8,192 rows of the held-out temporal test window, the last 30 percent of the transactions in time order (2022-09-07 14:55 to 2022-09-18 16:18), which the model was not fitted, tuned or calibrated on. Their 32 features are computed by the training script's own functions, exactly as it computes them for test rows: per-account aggregates causal, so each row sees only earlier transactions, and structural features from the rows before the test window. Checked when this file was built: the published graph scores AUPRC 0.1233 over all 1,523,504 rows of that window, the figure the registry records. Unlike the 8-feature PaySim sample this page uses for the FHE/MPC pipeline. The identical rows the gradient-boosting teacher's sample ships, with the 79 per-transaction features added.
split: the rows of finance_aml.gbm's sample, a draw from the held-out temporal test window, the last 30 percent of the transactions in time order, enriched to 2 percent laundering, with the 79 per-transaction features added
attribution: Altman et al., 'Realistic Synthetic Financial Transactions for Anti-Money Laundering Models', NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks. Data: IBM Transactions for Anti-Money Laundering (AML), CDLA-Sharing-1.0.
modifications: The rows of finance_aml.gbm's sample: its 32 features computed from the published transactions, enriched to 2 percent laundering, plus 79 per-transaction window features computed by the training script.

input.layout: samples[i] is one transaction's 111 engineered features, raw: the graph scales them itself

expected.note: On these rows, enriched to 2 percent laundering, minority-class F1 is 0.5259. The record's 0.3350 is over the whole test window at its real prevalence, so the two are not comparable, and this sample checks that the browser reproduces the graph.
